use_when.text: Use it on Back Office dashboards for numbers staff check every day.
Put three or four cards in a row with the same width.
Write the Label as a short noun phrase, such as Open reports.
Write the Delta as a change with a time, such as +12 since yesterday.
Turn off Show delta when there is nothing to compare.

dont_use_when.text: Do not put more than one number in a card.
Do not use it for text that is not a number.
Do not use colour alone to show whether a change is good or bad.
Do not mix card widths in the same row.
Do not recolour it outside the bound tokens.

best_practice.text: Order cards by what staff act on first, such as Claims pending before Returned.
Round large numbers, such as 1.2k, only when the exact count does not matter.

a11y.text:
Renders a
with no role holding three

elements in order: Label, Value, Delta.
Not interactive: no button, link or tabindex.
Read the card as one sentence, such as "Open reports, 128, up 12 since yesterday".
Write changes in words where they matter, since "+" and "−" can be read inconsistently.
Use a heading, or a dt and dd pair, so the label and value stay linked.
If the number updates live, announce changes with aria-live="polite".
Label, value and delta text are above 4.5:1 on the card background.

differences.detail:
Figma asks for a heading, or a dt and dd pair, so the label and value stay linked. The code renders Label and Value as two sibling

elements with no heading and no dt/dd.

gaps.detail: Stat Card has no union-typed variant prop in code (StatCard.tsx:3-12: Label, Value, Delta, boolean "Show delta"), so there is nothing to describe.
No story renders Stat Card inside another component, and its own stories show it alone.
Stat Card composes no other component and no story pairs it with a sibling component.
